newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warship headed for Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warship headed for Sierra Leone.

text.p: The U.S. Navy helicopter ship Kearsarge is steaming toward Sierra Leone with 1,200 Marines but the military has received no request to evacuate Americans from the West African nation, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

U.S. Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said the situation in Sierra Leone was calm after a weekend military coup that ousted the elected government. But he said the Kearsarge would be offshore within 24 to 48 hours and "ready to conduct contingency operations if necessary."

The new army rulers in Sierra Leone, where there are some 400 Americans in the capital Freetown, have said they have opened land borders and air and seaports. But a dusk to dawn curfew remains in force.

Bacon said the Kearsarge left Atlantic waters off Zaire, where it had been on stand-by for a possible evacuation from Kinshasa, on Saturday night and would stop off Sierra Leone on its way to its regular station in the Mediterranean.

"It is planning to stop probably 20 or so miles off the shore and wait and see what happens," he told reporters. "There has been a (State Department) request for us to be available if necessary, but no request to be more than available."
Bacon said there were thousands of other foreigners in Sierra Leone, including U.N. workers, but the Pentagon had received no requests so far for any evacuations.
